Which Velama ruler, who attempted to win territories from the Vijayanagara, ended his career in failure in this endeavour?
Which work does Madiki Singana draw a verse from, enjoining the king to be thorough in the sapta upayas (seven strategies)?
According to Sukranitisara, how many members were prescribed for the council of ministers?
What was the head of the council of ministers called?
In which work does Madiki Singana devote a chapter titled Durga Samrakshanamu, discussing the importance and defence of forts?
Which of the following were the main hill forts (giri durgas) of the Recherla Velamas?
faqs.e: Orugallu, Amanagallu, Anathagiri, Aruvapally, Podichedy, Anumula, Pangal, and Jallipalli were the land forts (sthala durgas) of the Recherla Velamas.

faqs.q: The Draksharama inscription refers to Anapota by which title?
Who was the head man of the village in the administrative divisions of the Rachakonda and Devarakonda Velama kingdoms?
faqs.e: Karanam was the village accountant maintaining land records and tax rates; Bari kapu was the village policeman.

faqs.q: Under Mada Nayaka I (1361–1384 A.D.), which Brahmin minister was regarded as Rajyangaika durandhrah (expert in statecraft) and Kavivaa (best among poets)?

Consider the following statements regarding the Sayampet inscription of Rao Dharma Nayaka (1429 A.D.):
(I) It refers to 12 virtues/shares of a village given to Brahmins.
(II) It indicates that gifts to individual Brahmins were no longer necessary or dharmically appropriate as before.
(III) It shows that gifts to Brahmins became tied to the sectarian nexus of bhakti-centred Hinduism.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Unlike the Kakatiyas, Chalukyas, and Rastrakutas who claimed descent from the lunar race, the Velamas of Rachakonda and Devarakonda claimed equality with which lineage?
faqs.e: Their subordinate rulers of Jallipalli were, however, called Soma Vamsa Kshatriyas.

faqs.q: The Vaisyas, locally called Komatis, were organized into a caste-cum-professional guild known as 'Nakaram' at eighteen different places, with headquarters at which town?
faqs.e: Penugonda is located in the West Godavari district.

faqs.q: Which guild, whose members were mentioned as Balanjasettikandru, competed with the Vaisyas and by the 15th century had absorbed them, indicating a decline in the itinerant nature of Vaisya trade?
The Panchamas, constituting the bulk of the lowest social stratum, comprised which two communities?
faqs.e: Malas constituted agricultural labour, while Madigas prepared accessories for agriculture and were employed for executing animal sacrifices.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the position of women, per contemporary works like the Rukmangada Charitra:
(I) A wife should not be angry even if her husband desires the company of another woman.
(II) If the husband dies, the wife should jump into the funeral pyre.
(III) Widows were held in high regard and honoured by society.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The widow was described as the most miserable of all — an object of ridicule, whose blessings were considered poison by law, and whom society spurned.

faqs.q: Which wife of Alaraju committed Sati when her husband was poisoned to death by Nayakuralu of Palanadu?
During the Velama regions of Rachakonda and Devarakonda, the era witnessed the growth of which two religious traditions in Telangana?
During Kakatiya times, which of the following were centres of Vaishnavism?
The growth of the Vijayanagaras, who patronaged which cult, would have necessitated the Velama kings to extend patronage to the Vaishnava cult in the region?
Vedanta Desika of Srirangam was perhaps preceptor of Venna, son of which Velama ruler?

Consider the following pairs regarding the two schools of Vaishnavism that crystallized through the efforts of the Srirangam acharyas:
(I) Vadagalai – northern school – led by Vedanta Desika
(II) Tengalai – southern school – led by Pillai Lokacharya
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
Which deity was stated in the Ayanavolu inscription to be the Kuladevata (tutelary deity) of the Velamas — contradicting the traditional scholarly view that they were staunch Vaishnavites?
faqs.e: This is cited as evidence that, like other medieval power groups, the Velama kings tried to stabilize their hegemony through royal temple policy by extending patronage to popular cults broadly, rather than being exclusively Vaishnavite.

faqs.q: Prior to Kakatiya rule, inscriptions issued by feudatories and local chiefs mostly recorded which form of donation to temples, rather than monetary grants?
faqs.e: Post-Kakatiya-period inscriptions issued by feudal lords began referring to monetary grants alongside land grants, indirectly reflecting the growth of a monetary economy.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding villages held by the state under Rachakonda and Devarakonda administration:
(I) Villages held directly by the state, where revenue was collected by its own administrative machinery, were called Bhandaaravada gramas or kara villages.
(II) The Mohammedan rulers called these Khalsa or Khas lands.
(III) Villages held by feudatories rendering military service were called Nayaka villages and were hereditary.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Nayaka villages were NOT hereditary — the emperor could confiscate these holdings at any time.

faqs.q: In the Domalapally inscription of Mada I (1367 A.D.), which term denotes wet land under a canal?
faqs.e: Velibhumi denoted dry land in the same inscription.

faqs.q: Which land measure, mentioned in the Domalapally inscription of Mada I, was equal to the modern acre?
faqs.e: Both Nivart and Maruthuu were used as land measures generally equivalent to the modern acre; Tumu, mentioned in the Kandikonda inscription of Venna, was a separate measure of land.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding irrigation in the Rachakonda and Devarakonda region:
(I) The Telangana region is a rain shadow area with a limited river system.
(II) Only the river Krishna touches the region's peripheral zones, with Dindi, Musi, and Aleru as its tributaries.
(III) About 20 inscriptions belonging to Velama kings referring to tanks/wells were found in the region, of which at least four are fragmented.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Which tank was constructed by Anapota I in 1365 A.D., alongside 2 wells, at Rachakonda?
Sarvajna Singama II, son of Anapota I, composed which of the following Sanskrit works?

options.a: Rasarnava Sudhakaram, Ratna Panchalika, and Sangeeta Sudhakaram

faqs.a: Rasarnava Sudhakaram, Ratna Panchalika, and Sangeeta Sudhakaram

faqs.q: Rao Madha Naya, son of Sarvajna Singama II, wrote which Sanskrit commentary on the Ramayana?
Which Sanskrit poet of Anapota I wrote Madanavilasa bhanamu?
Visveshwara, court poet of Singamabhupala II, wrote a book on Alankara Sastra titled Chamatkara Chandrika, in which he described Sarvagna II by which epithet?
faqs.e: The epithet means "sculptor in literature."

faqs.q: Sakalya Mallubattu, court poet of Singama Nayaka III, is also known by which title meaning "poet-grandfather in four languages"?
Sakalya Ayyalarya, grandson of Sakalya Mallubattu, was the laureate writer of the Bhaskara Ramayanam at the court of which ruler?

Consider the following pairs of Telugu poets and their works during the Velama kingdom period:
(I) Gaurana – Navanatha Charitra and Harichandropakhyanam
(II) Koravi Goparaju – Simhasana Dvatrimsika
(III) Bammara Pothana – Bhogini Dandakam, Andhramaha Bharatham, and Veerabhadra Vijayam
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
Which Telugu poet worked on Vishnupuranam, a work that also describes the victories of the Velama kings?
Machaldevi, the courtesan of the last Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra, is said to have maintained Chitrasalas (painting museums) in which city?
faqs.e: This is described in the work Kridabhiramam.

faqs.q: In his greatest work Maha Bhagavatam, poet Potana vividly described the process of mixing how many important colours used for paintings?

Consider the following statements regarding the Ramanavami paintings discovered in a temple in Rachakonda:
(I) Their concept appears to have been drawn from the contemporary work Ranganatha Ramayanam.
(II) The paintings were found in the temple located inside the south-east entrance of the fort.
(III) Bahamani Sultans had most of the paintings chiseled out, as decorations were treated as against Shariat law.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
The Rachakonda temple paintings are dated to roughly 650 years ago, based on an inscription of 1365 A.D. by which ruler, found in front of the temple of Rama?
The Padmanayakas held a unique title, Astadika raya, indicating that they had conquered how many cardinal points of the kingdom?
faqs.e: These points were bounded by sculptures of Hanuman, Ganesh, and Bhairava on boulders, usually near fort entrance gates.

faqs.q: At Pandavulagutta in Warangal district, the cave complex's ending point, containing pre-historic and historic paintings, is called by which name?
faqs.e: "Gonthemma" is stated to be the corrupt form of "Kunti," mother of the Pandavas of Vaishnava faith.

faqs.q: The gravitational suction technology for drinking water, later adapted by the Rachakonda Velamas and Golconda, was first used in India by which ruler in the 11th century?
faqs.e: This was inside the tank bund of Bhopal Lake and on a stream in Bhojpur, Madhya Pradesh, utilizing architectural features from Bhoja's work Samaraanagana Sutradhaara.

faqs.q: Which two lakes, constructed by Anapota Nayaka in 1368 A.D. at Rachakonda, supplied drinking water to the palaces via a corbelled canal using gravitational technology?

options.c: Parvata Rao Tatakamu and Naga Samudram
options.d: Durgam Cheruvu and Madha Rao Cheruvu

faqs.q: The most important and earliest temple in Rachakonda fort — the Ramalayam — was built in 1365 A.D. by which ruler?
The Vaishnavite temple at Naganayakonda Fort is confirmed as Vaishnavite based on which unique architectural feature of the Padmanayaka period?

options.a: Dvarapala sculptures of Hanuman and Garuda on either side
options.c: A Kalyana Mandapam to the north

faqs.a: Dvarapala sculptures of Hanuman and Garuda on either side
